name: Horne-Horowitz Charged Black String in Three Dimensions
description: A straight black string in three spacetime dimensions carrying an axion charge, an exact solution of string theory built from a gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model. Like the charged black hole of Reissner and Nordström it has an event horizon, an inner horizon, and a timelike singularity, and with no charge it is Witten's black hole of two dimensions times a line.

history: James H. Horne began the construction of this string at the Aspen Center for Physics, and Horne and Gary T. Horowitz wrote it up at the University of California, Santa Barbara, in a preprint dated July 1991 [horne1992black]. Edward Witten had just found a black hole in two dimensions in the Wess-Zumino-Witten model on the group $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with a one dimensional subgroup gauged [witten1991]. Horne and Horowitz added a free boson $x$ to the model and gauged the same subgroup together with a translation of $x$, and obtained an exact conformal field theory of a straight, static string with an event horizon [horne1992black]. The string carries a mass $M$ and an axion charge $Q$ per unit length, and its string metric at lowest order in $1/k$ is $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \frac{M}{r}\right)dt^2 + \left(1 - \frac{Q^2}{Mr}\right)dx^2 + \left(1 - \frac{M}{r}\right)^{-1}\left(1 - \frac{Q^2}{Mr}\right)^{-1}\frac{k\,dr^2}{8r^2},$$ with an antisymmetric tensor field $H_{rtx} = Q/r^2$ and a dilaton $\Phi = \ln r + \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(k/2)$ [horne1992black].¶The static charged black holes of David Garfinkle, Horowitz, and Andrew Strominger have a spacelike singularity and no inner horizon [horne1992black]. For $0 < |Q| < M$ this string, in Horne and Horowitz's words, "has a regular inner horizon (in addition to the event horizon) and a timelike singularity" [horne1992black]. The event horizon is at $r = M$ and the inner horizon at $r = Q^2/M$, and the causal structure follows that of the charged black hole of Hans Reissner and Gunnar Nordström, region by region [horne1992black]. In the Reissner-Nordström hole the Killing vector that translates time far away is timelike again inside the inner horizon; here $\partial_t$ stays spacelike all the way to the singularity, and $\partial_x$, the translation along the string, is timelike inside the inner horizon [horne1992black]. Each point of Horne and Horowitz's diagram is therefore a line along $x$ outside the inner horizon and a line along $t$ inside it [horne1992black]. Timelike geodesics turn back before $r = 0$, so no freely falling observer reaches the singularity, and a light ray with momentum $P$ along the string and energy $E$ reaches it only when $P^2M^2 > E^2Q^2$ [horne1992black].¶With no charge the field $H$ vanishes and the string is Witten's black hole times a line [horne1992black, witten1991]. The Hawking temperature, $T = \sqrt{(M^2 - Q^2)/2k}\,/\pi M$, falls to zero as $|Q|$ approaches $M$, and in that limit, in Horne and Horowitz's words, "the event horizon remains but the singularity disappears" [horne1992black]. At $|Q| = M$ the coordinate $\rho$, with $\rho^2 = r - M$, runs through the horizon from positive to negative values into a copy of the region outside, and observers who cross it, "fortunately for them", find themselves in a second asymptotically flat region identical to the first [horne1992black]. With $r$, $t$, and $x$ rescaled as $|Q|$ goes to $M$, the limit is anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions with a constant dilaton, the ungauged model on $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ [horne1992black]. For $|Q| > M$ there is neither a horizon nor a curvature singularity, and identifying $x$ with period $\pi|Q|\sqrt{2k/(Q^2 - M^2)}$ removes a conical singularity at the centre and makes each slice of constant $t$ an infinite cigar [horne1992black].¶The constant $k$ is the level of the gauged model, whose central charge, $3k/(k - 2)$, is one more than that of Witten's black hole for the added boson [horne1992black, horowitz1993]. The low energy equations contain a cosmological term $8/k$ in the dilaton equation, and the displayed metric solves those equations for each $k$ [horne1992black]. A bosonic string needs a total central charge of 26, so $k = 52/23$ for this string alone, the value Horowitz and Dean L. Welch gave in 1993, and with a larger $k$ part of the central charge comes from an internal conformal field theory [horne1992black, horowitz1993]. Rescaled by the dilaton to the metric of Einstein's action, the string has both horizons and is asymptotically flat, but the symmetry that is timelike outside the horizon approaches a boost at infinity, so in that frame the string is not static [horne1992black].¶Horne, Horowitz, and Alan R. Steif showed later in 1991 that the duality of string theory along a direction of translation exchanges the momentum in that direction with the axion charge [horne1992momentum]. The uncharged string of mass $M_0$, boosted along $x$ with rapidity $\alpha$ and then dualized, becomes the charged string with $M = M_0\cosh^2\alpha$ and $Q = M_0\cosh\alpha\sinh\alpha$, so when $x$ is a circle the charged string is equivalent to a boosted uncharged one, which has a spacelike singularity and no inner horizon [horne1992momentum]. They argued from that equivalence that the exact string background has no inner horizon, although its low energy metric does [horne1992momentum]. Paul H. Ginsparg and Fernando Quevedo related the axial and vector gaugings in 1992, mapping a regular surface of the uncharged geometry to the curvature singularity of the charged string through a choice of duality direction [ginsparg1992duality].¶Konstadinos Sfetsos computed the metric and dilaton of the gauged model to all orders in $1/k$ in 1992, finding a second curvature singularity at finite $k$ that merges with the one at $r = 0$ as $k$ grows without bound [sfetsos1993exact]. The inner horizon remains in those field variables [sfetsos1993exact]. Garfinkle added waves of arbitrary profile travelling along the extremal string in 1992, using its null Killing symmetry without changing the dilaton or antisymmetric tensor [garfinkle1992]. Abbas Ali and Alok Kumar embedded the rotating black hole of Máximo Bañados, Claudio Teitelboim, and Jorge Zanelli in string theory in a preprint dated December 1992 and used an $O(2,2)$ transformation to obtain a moving uncharged string [banados1992, ali1993duality].¶Horowitz and Welch dualized the nonextremal rotating hole along its angle into this charged string in 1993, with the string charge equal to half the angular momentum of the hole [horowitz1993]. The extremal hole has a different dual, an extremal black string carrying a travelling wave [horowitz1993]. Horowitz and Welch showed that duality preserves the Hawking temperature for the same horizon generator and the horizon area in the Einstein metric, with the period of the dual direction included, in 1993 [horowitz1994duality]. Itzhak Bars and Sfetsos recovered the finite $k$ metric and dilaton from a quantum effective action in 1993, restricting the calculation to the zero modes [bars1993effective].¶Sfetsos and Arkady A. Tseytlin checked the charged background against the conditions for conformal invariance at two worldsheet loops in 1993 and obtained a gauge invariant antisymmetric tensor [sfetsos1994tensor]. By redefining the local background fields they also made the lowest order geometry solve those equations; the propagation equations for string modes change form with the field variables [sfetsos1994tensor]. David Gershon derived duality transformations for the metric and dilaton at finite $k$ in December 1993 and recovered the charged string from the ungauged model [gershon1994exact]. Welch dualized the nonextremal string along time in 1994 and obtained a boosted uncharged string of negative mass; the extremal string maps to a plane wave of negative energy [welch1994timelike]. Horowitz and Arkady A. Tseytlin obtained the extremal string directly by gauging a different subgroup in 1994 and absorbed its corrections in $1/k$ into coordinate rescalings [horowitz1994exact].¶Warren G. Anderson and Nemanja Kaloper added electric charge in 1995 and obtained two families with different extremal limits, including solutions with an ergoregion and a causally geodesically complete interior [anderson1995strings]. Mikhail Z. Iofa calculated a correction from the torus worldsheet in 1996 and found that the mass integral diverges at spatial infinity before subtraction of the asymptotic contribution [iofa1997genus]. Jeongwon Ho, Wontae Kim, and Young-Jai Park showed in 1998 that duality preserves the entropy and local temperature at a finite boundary and transforms the combined work terms in the first law consistently [ho1998quasilocal].¶Yun Soo Myung and coauthors found no growing exterior dilaton mode in 1998 when the coupled perturbations obey their horizon and asymptotic regularity conditions [lee1998stability]. Kaloper counted states of the conformal field theory near the extremal horizon in 1998 and recovered the entropy of a regulated elementary segment [kaloper1998entropy]. The segment grows without bound as the temperature vanishes; its entropy stays finite in that limit even though the entropy per unit length vanishes [kaloper1998entropy]. Soon-Tae Hong and coauthors embedded the exterior of the neutral string in a flat space with four dimensions and the charged exterior in one with five dimensions in 2001 [hong2001embedding].¶Stéphane Detournay, Domenico Orlando, P. Marios Petropoulos, and Philippe Spindel obtained the string and electrically charged extensions from current deformations of the model on $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ in 2005 [detournay2005deformed]. They calculated the conformal weights of the primary states in the deformed theories [detournay2005deformed]. Eloy Ayón-Beato and Gastón Giribet showed in 2007 that the nonextremal charged string is its own dual along an oblique spacelike Killing direction of constant norm [ayon2007selfdual]. Seungjoon Hyun, Jaehoon Jeong, Wontae Kim, and John J. Oh formed the neutral string by collapse of an inhomogeneous dust cloud in 2007 and determined the interior numerically near the boundary [hyun2007collapse].¶Roberto Emparan, Daniel Grumiller, and Kentaro Tanabe found this string in 2013 as the geometry near the horizon of black branes with an electric string charge and no dilaton, in the limit of a large number of dimensions [emparan2013strings]. José Daniel Edelstein and coauthors added terms with four derivatives to the gravitational action in 2018 and calculated the corresponding corrections to the nonextremal string and its duality map [edelstein2018duality]. The Hawking temperature and entropy remain equal on the two sides to first order in the added couplings, with the same horizon generator and compatible coordinate periods [edelstein2018duality]. Spindel found perturbations of the metric, dilaton, and gauge fields that grow exponentially with time in 2018 and constructed time dependent solutions with those boundary conditions [spindel2019instability]. A cosmological singularity forms at the future boundary of those solutions, at the Cauchy horizon of the stationary string [spindel2019instability].¶Detournay, Petropoulos, and Céline Zwikel constructed another space of allowed asymptotic fields in 2019, including the original string when the electromagnetic field vanishes [detournay2019symmetries]. The corresponding conserved charges obey a Virasoro algebra without a central term and three global $u(1)$ symmetries [detournay2019symmetries]. Yongwan Gim and Kim treated the cosmological constant as a thermodynamic pressure in 2019 and obtained an extended first law and a Smarr relation for an elementary string segment [gim2019pressure]. Luis Apolo, Detournay, and Wei Song reached the string in 2020 from the rotating hole through a duality, a shift, and a second duality, with an additional constant shift of the antisymmetric tensor potential [apolo2020black]. With the spatial direction compact and the charge fixed, they identified the string with a thermal state of a conformal field theory deformed by the single trace operator $T\bar{T}$ [apolo2020black].¶Soumangsu Chakraborty, Amit Giveon, and David Kutasov followed the positive deformation of this thermal family in 2020 and obtained a density of states that crosses from Cardy growth to Hagedorn growth at high energy [chakraborty2020negative]. Sibylle Driezen and Konstantinos Sfetsos constructed integrable deformations of the Euclidean string in 2021 [driezen2021lambda]. The deformed theories have running couplings and remain related by axial and vector duality as canonically equivalent systems [driezen2021lambda]. Hwajin Eom and Kim determined the collapsing neutral dust interior analytically in 2022, extending the numerical construction of Hyun and coauthors [eom2022collapse]. Ali Eghbali and coauthors retained both horizon radii in their chosen field variables when they calculated the first correction in the inverse string tension to the angular dual of the rotating hole in 2022 [eghbali2022duality].¶Ho, Kim, and Bum-Hoon Lee tested strong cosmic censorship in 2022 with a massive scalar coupled to the dilaton on the fixed string geometry [ho2022strong]. They found locally square integrable first derivatives at the inner horizon for sufficiently massive fields near extremality, violating strong cosmic censorship in that linear test [ho2022strong]. First derivatives of the massless field are not locally square integrable at the inner horizon over the range studied [ho2022strong]. Shuxuan Ying modelled corrections in the inverse string tension with a resummation matching the known low orders in 2023 and obtained regular interiors of the neutral string [ying2023alpha]. Ying also made the neutral interior regular with a chosen nonlocal dilaton potential modelling string loop effects in 2023 [ying2023regular].¶Eghbali, Simin Ghasemi-Sorkhabi, and Adel Rezaei-Aghdam kept the charged string metric and axion field in generalized supergravity in 2024 by adding a Killing vector and changing the dilaton and cosmological term [eghbali2024generalized]. Meseret Asrat obtained a rotating family containing this string at a restricted parameter value in 2025 [asrat2025strings]. Detournay, José Figueroa, and Alejandro Vilar López extended the classical duality map to asymptotic fields in 2025, starting with the boundary conditions for the nonextremal rotating hole [detournay2025asymptotic]. The resulting string phase space has four infinite towers of charges and contains Bondi-Metzner-Sachs algebras in two and three dimensions [detournay2025asymptotic]. Ziyi Li decomposed the Euclidean gauged model into characters and extracted the spacetime spectrum of its smooth horizonless continuation in October 2026 [li2026spectra]. Li continued only the unflowed sector to the Lorentzian black string [li2026spectra].

related.text: Witten's black hole of two dimensions, the cross section of this string when it carries no charge. Horne and Horowitz built the charged string by adding a line to Witten's model and gauging a translation along it [horne1992black].

The charged black hole of general relativity, with the same diagram of horizons and singularity. Inside its inner horizon the time translation is timelike again, and here the translation along the string takes that role [horne1992black].

The rotating black hole of three dimensions with a negative cosmological constant. Dualized along its angle it becomes this string, its angular momentum turned into twice the string's charge and its horizons at the same radii [horowitz1993].

Schwarzschild's black hole stretched along a line, a static black string of general relativity, which needs five dimensions or more when matter obeys the strong energy condition [horne1992black, horowitz1991]. This one is a solution in three, where the dilaton and antisymmetric field of its string metric violate that condition [horne1992black].
The charged black hole of string theory in four dimensions, with one horizon and no inner horizon for every charge. Its singularity is spacelike, and the string's is timelike [horne1992black].

In the limit $|Q| \to M$ with $r$, $t$, and $x$ rescaled, the string becomes anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions with a constant dilaton, the ungauged model on $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ [horne1992black].

coordinates.name: Static

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Axion charge per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, r)$, with $x$ along the string and $r$ fixed by the dilaton, $\Phi = \ln r + \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(k/2)$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} - \dfrac{4\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}{k\,r^2}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{4Q^2\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}{M^2\,k\,r^2}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{M^2 - 2M\,r + Q^2}{2\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Wess-Zumino-Witten

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Axion charge per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(u, v)$ of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ in which the model is gauged, with $r = M - (M^2 - Q^2)uv/M$ and, outside the event horizon, $u/v = -e^{2\kappa t}$, $\kappa = \sqrt{2(M^2 - Q^2)/k}/M$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\dfrac{k\left(Q^2v^2\,du^2 + Q^2u^2\,dv^2 + 2\left(2M^2 - (2M^2 - Q^2)uv\right)du\,dv\right)}{8(1 - uv)\left(M^2 - (M^2 - Q^2)uv\right)} + \dfrac{(M^2 - Q^2)(1 - uv)}{M^2 - (M^2 - Q^2)uv}\,dx^2

nonzero.value: -\dfrac{2Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
\dfrac{2Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
-\dfrac{2Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
\dfrac{2Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
-\dfrac{4Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
\dfrac{4Q^2\left(Q^2\,u\,v - M^2 - M^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}

geodesics: \ddot{u} + \dfrac{v\left(3Q^4\,u\,v - 4Q^4\,u^2\,v^2 + 4M^2\,Q^2 - 12M^2\,Q^2\,u\,v + 8M^2\,Q^2\,u^2\,v^2 - 4M^4 + 8M^4\,u\,v - 4M^4\,u^2\,v^2\right)}{4\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{Q^2\,u\left(2M^2\,u\,v - 2M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{u}\dot{v} - \dfrac{Q^4\,u^3}{4\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{v}^2 + \dfrac{2Q^2\,u\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{x}^2 = 0

\ddot{v} - \dfrac{Q^4\,v^3}{4\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{Q^2\,v\left(2M^2\,u\,v - 2M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{u}\dot{v} + \dfrac{u\left(3Q^4\,u\,v - 4Q^4\,u^2\,v^2 + 4M^2\,Q^2 - 12M^2\,Q^2\,u\,v + 8M^2\,Q^2\,u^2\,v^2 - 4M^4 + 8M^4\,u\,v - 4M^4\,u^2\,v^2\right)}{4\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{v}^2 + \dfrac{2Q^2\,v\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{x}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Axion charge per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, x, r)$, with the advanced time $dv = dt + \sqrt{k/8}\,dr/\left(r(1 - M/r)\sqrt{1 - Q^2/(Mr)}\right)$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} - \dfrac{4\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}{k\,r^2}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{M}\sqrt{M\,r - Q^2}}{\sqrt{k}\,r^{3/2}}\dot{v}\dot{r} + \dfrac{4Q^2\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}{M^2\,k\,r^2}\dot{x}^2 + \dfrac{Q^2 - 2M\,r}{2r\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Extremal

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \rho)$ at $|Q| = M$, with $\rho^2 = r - M$.

coordinates.name: Extremal Interior

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \rho)$ inside the horizon at $|Q| = M$, with $\rho^2 = M - r$.

coordinates.name: Superextremal

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Axion charge per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \rho)$ at $|Q| > M$, with $\rho^2 = r - Q^2/M$ and $x$ of period $\pi|Q|\sqrt{2k/(Q^2 - M^2)}$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\dfrac{Q^2 - M^2 + M\rho^2}{Q^2 + M\rho^2}dt^2 + \dfrac{M\rho^2}{Q^2 + M\rho^2}dx^2 + \dfrac{Mk\,d\rho^2}{2\left(Q^2 - M^2 + M\rho^2\right)}
geodesics: \ddot{\rho} + \dfrac{2M^2\,\rho\left(Q^2 + M\,\rho^2 - M^2\right)}{k\left(M\,\rho^2 + Q^2\right)^2}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{2Q^2\,\rho\left(M^2 - M\,\rho^2 - Q^2\right)}{k\left(M\,\rho^2 + Q^2\right)^2}\dot{x}^2 + \dfrac{M\,\rho}{M^2 - M\,\rho^2 - Q^2}\dot{\rho}^2 = 0
